inspection_summary: Inspected all 1,517 logical lines. The source develops a coherent chain from symmetry-class predictions for L-function moments, through random-matrix formulas for the universal constants g_lambda, to mollified-moment diagnostics, Barnes double-gamma continuation, integer and p-adic structure, self-similar valuation limits, and large-index asymptotics. Formula extraction is imperfect but most mechanisms are recoverable from checked prose and adjoining equations; only the graph-only regions lack usable visual content.

sections_inspected.label: Front matter and abstract
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: States the central hypothesis that symmetry type governs both zero statistics and mean values, and previews the Barnes double-gamma and self-similarity connections.

sections_inspected.label: 1. Introduction
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Factors moment conjectures into family arithmetic and symmetry-dependent components, defines the roles of g_k and B(k), and compares orthogonal, symplectic, and unitary families.

sections_inspected.label: 2. Statement of Results
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Transfers random-matrix characteristic-polynomial limits to formulas for g_lambda and previews their analytic, integral, p-adic, and self-similar consequences.

sections_inspected.label: 3. Mollified mean squares
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Uses a common mollifier construction to expose symmetry-specific responses and an orthogonal/symplectic derivative correspondence.

sections_inspected.label: 4. Meromorphicity of g_lambda
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Locates poles, proves nonvanishing meromorphic order two, and represents normalized g_lambda with Gamma and the Barnes-Vigneras double Gamma function.

sections_inspected.label: 5. Integrality results
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Converts random-matrix limits to finite factorial products, then to p-adic floor-sum formulas whose termwise nonnegativity proves integrality and prime-support restrictions.

sections_inspected.label: 6. The function c_p
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Encodes normalized p-adic valuations by a continuous scale-invariant distance-to-integers series and analyzes its rational-point self-similarity, cusps, and vertical tangents.

sections_inspected.label: 7. Asymptotics
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Derives large-k expansions for all three symmetry constants from factorial products and Euler-Maclaurin summation, closing the double-Gamma identification.

sections_inspected.label: References and affiliation
sections_inspected.mathematical_role: Bibliographic and publication metadata; no additional mathematical argument.

accepted_units.title: Symmetry type as a common governor of zeros and mean values

accepted_units.context_note: The abstract and opening paragraphs jointly establish the transfer being tested; neither alone gives the full contrast.

accepted_units.title: The universal factor g_k measures the gap beyond a length-T Dirichlet polynomial
accepted_units.why_material: Separates the arithmetic Euler-product factor a_k from g_k and gives g_k an operational meaning as how many length-T polynomial approximations are needed to capture the moment.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the moment normalization, the Montgomery-Vaughan length restriction, and the comparison polynomial; these are all needed for the interpretation.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate: key formulas are text-layer readable, while some typography should be checked against the scan before reuse.

accepted_units.title: A parameter dictionary for family mean-value conjectures
accepted_units.why_material: Distinguishes symmetry-controlled g_k and B(k), family-specific arithmetic a_k, and functional-equation scaling A in a reusable family template.
accepted_units.context_note: The preceding small-k examples motivate the abstraction; the span ends before specializing to a symmetry class.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate: the template formula has extraction noise, but every parameter's role is explicit in prose.

accepted_units.title: Orthogonal symmetry produces the k(k-1)/2 moment exponent
accepted_units.why_material: Connects a concrete class of self-dual L-function families to the orthogonal moment exponent, central-value parity behavior, and functional-equation scaling.

accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate: family lists and explanatory prose are clear, while displayed conjectures carry formula-layout risk.

accepted_units.title: Symplectic symmetry changes the exponent to k(k+1)/2
accepted_units.why_material: Shows how a different symmetry class changes the universal moment exponent while retaining the same functional-equation rule for A.
accepted_units.context_note: Immutable v1 span is coherent and includes examples, a representative conjecture, and the parameter conclusion.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate: classification prose is reliable; displayed constants and exponents should retain source-image provenance.

accepted_units.title: Unitary moments complete the O-Sp-U parameter comparison
accepted_units.why_material: Completes the symmetry trichotomy with |L|^{2k}, B(k)=k^2, doubled conductor scaling, and the interpretation of zeta shifts as a unitary family.
accepted_units.context_note: Also separates the family arithmetic factor from the still-mysterious g_k and introduces the random-matrix route.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate: prose fixes the comparison despite imperfect product-formula extraction.

accepted_units.title: Characteristic-polynomial limits predict the universal constants
accepted_units.why_material: Maps each symmetry type to a large-rank Gamma-product limit and explains why the Gamma(1+B(lambda)) normalization is retained to preserve arithmetic meaning and integral special values.
accepted_units.context_note: The GUE motivation and three parallel limit formulas form one comparison unit.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: exact product factors depend on displayed formulas and require scan verification, but the transfer and normalization rationale are explicit.

accepted_units.title: Analytic continuation at lambda=1/2 predicts a constrained zeta moment
accepted_units.why_material: Uses a nonintegral random-matrix constant to make a numerical first-moment prediction and compares it with an RH-conditional bound.
accepted_units.context_note: A compact calibration example linking analytic continuation to an independently constrained quantity.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: the closed formula is visually fragile, though the numerical value and inequality are recoverable.

accepted_units.title: A common reciprocal-polynomial mollifier and the unitary response
accepted_units.why_material: Defines a family-independent mollifier from coefficients of L(s)^{-1}, then gives the unitary quadratic functional that exposes how mollifier length enters.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the boundary conditions on the polynomial and the simple test P=x, Q=1.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: the structural construction is clear, but the exact double-integral functional requires formula verification.

accepted_units.title: The orthogonal short-mollifier limit is anomalous
accepted_units.why_material: Shows that the orthogonal mollified mean square has a qualitatively unexpected limit as mollifier length shrinks, suggesting sensitivity to low-lying zeros.
accepted_units.context_note: The anomaly depends on the displayed orthogonal functional and its simple specialization.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: exact differential terms are formula-dependent; the limiting behavior and interpretation are explicit in prose.

accepted_units.title: Differentiation interchanges symplectic and orthogonal mollified responses
accepted_units.why_material: Identifies M_Sp(P,Q',theta) with M_O(P,Q,theta), turning previously observed coincidences between distinct nonvanishing arguments into a symmetry-level operator relation.
accepted_units.context_note: Includes the symplectic setup, parity distinction, antiderivative notation, and the stated correspondence.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate: the exact functionals are formula-sensitive, but the derivative correspondence is unambiguous.

accepted_units.title: Pole data and growth identify normalized g_lambda with double Gamma expressions
accepted_units.why_material: Packages nonvanishing, order, pole multiplicities, Barnes double-Gamma representations, and cross-symmetry identities into an analytic continuation of the universal constants.
accepted_units.context_note: Immutable v1 span retained; section heading and proof through line 605 are needed as repair context for derivational completeness.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: pole locations are readable, but exact constants in the Barnes formulas require scan verification.

accepted_units.title: A second Gamma difference controls meromorphic order
accepted_units.why_material: Rewrites the logarithm of the unitary product as a second finite difference of log Gamma, bounds it through a second-derivative estimate, and reads exact order from pole convergence.
accepted_units.context_note: The other symmetry cases are declared analogous; this span contains the complete illustrated mechanism.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate: enough equations survive to recover the proof architecture, though the integral remainder typography should be verified.

accepted_units.title: Finite factorial products expose integrality and prime support
accepted_units.why_material: States integrality and prime-divisor restrictions, gives finite factorial/double-factorial formulas for all symmetry types, and derives the unitary product from the random-matrix limit.
accepted_units.context_note: Immutable v1 span retained; the theorem's p-adic proof continues through line 884 and is supplied as repair context and a separate mechanism unit.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: precise products and zero-valuation intervals depend on displayed formulas, but the finite-product conversion is recoverable.

accepted_units.title: Floor-sum valuations prove integrality term by term
accepted_units.why_material: Regroups nested factorial products, derives exact p-adic floor-sum expressions, and proves every scale contribution is a nonnegative integer via a two-case residue analysis.
accepted_units.context_note: This is the missing proof support for the integrality theorem and also supplies the discrete formulas later scaled to c_p.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: several floor formulas are extraction-fragile, but the regrouping, scale decomposition, two cases, and nonnegativity conclusion are explicit.

accepted_units.title: Prime valuations converge to a scale-invariant distance series
accepted_units.why_material: Defines c_p by a bilateral distance-to-nearest-integer series, identifies it as the scaling limit of valuations, and classifies local behavior at rational points as self-similarity, cusp, or vertical tangent.
accepted_units.context_note: Immutable v1 span retained; the general series proposition and valuation-limit proof through line 1328 are necessary repair context.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: theorem statements are recoverable, but the exact local expansion for the rational-point classification needs formula verification.

accepted_units.title: A periodic seed generates a continuous discrete-scale covariant function
accepted_units.why_material: Abstracts c_p to a bilateral scale sum built from any suitably regular periodic seed and derives continuity, d(px)=p d(x), and the rational-point expansion used for the trichotomy.
accepted_units.context_note: The specialization f(x)=||x||^2 recovers the self-similarity, cusp, and vertical-tangent theorem.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: hypotheses and scaling law are clear; the full local expansion is formula-layout sensitive.

accepted_units.title: Split negative, intermediate, and tail scales to analyze local behavior
accepted_units.why_material: Proves the general scaling expansion by decomposing the bilateral series into three scale ranges and applying periodicity and Taylor expansion differently on each range.
accepted_units.context_note: This proof is reusable as a method for discrete-scale functions, independent of the specific distance seed.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: Moderate: prose clearly identifies the three ranges and tools; exact remainder coefficients are formula-sensitive.

accepted_units.title: Floor-valued p-adic sums converge to distance-to-integer energy
accepted_units.why_material: Unifies two valuation cases, rescales k=[p^j x], controls the infinite tails uniformly, and converts the limiting floor expression to ||p^ell x||^2.
accepted_units.context_note: The orthogonal and symplectic limits follow by the same representation and the cross-symmetry identity.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: the limit manipulations are visible but exact floor notation and indices need scan verification.

accepted_units.title: Symmetry-dependent constants have explicit large-k expansions
accepted_units.why_material: Gives distinct large-k expansions for unitary, orthogonal, and symplectic g_k and explains that their combination with Gamma asymptotics fixes the Barnes double-Gamma representations.
accepted_units.context_note: The theorem is mathematically substantive despite dense formula extraction.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: exact coefficients and lower-order terms require verification against the page image.

accepted_units.title: Factorial products reduce the asymptotics to four Euler-Maclaurin sums
accepted_units.why_material: Reduces all three large-k calculations to sums of log j, log(2j-1), j log j, and j log(2j-1), then supplies the expansions needed to close the proof.
accepted_units.context_note: This span records the calculational interface rather than repeating the large-k theorem.
accepted_units.representation_dependency: High: the reduction is clear, but exact constants in the four expansions are formula-dependent.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Symmetry predicts both moment growth and mollifier response
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: The O-Sp-U classification is reflected not only in moment exponents but also in distinct short-mollifier functionals, with differentiation explicitly bridging the orthogonal and symplectic cases.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The source gives conjectural family moments and selected mollified formulas, not a general theorem that symmetry alone determines every statistic.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: The universal moment constant bridges Dirichlet polynomials and random matrices
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: After separating family arithmetic and conductor scaling, g_k simultaneously measures failure of a single length-T Dirichlet polynomial to capture zeta moments and arises as a symmetry-specific characteristic-polynomial limit.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: This is a conceptual identification supported by matching conjectures; it is not an equality derived between the two models in the source.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: One random-matrix product has analytic, combinatorial, and p-adic faces
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Gamma-product limits analytically continue through the Barnes double Gamma function, collapse at integer parameters to factorial products, and then expose integrality, prime support, and large-k behavior.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: Exact displayed constants and some floor formulas are text-layer fragile and require image verification before formal reuse.

within_source_synthesis_candidates.title: Scale splitting converts discrete valuations into continuous fractal limits
within_source_synthesis_candidates.claim: Exact floor-sum valuations become a bilateral distance-to-integers energy after geometric rescaling; splitting scales then explains continuity, discrete covariance, and the rational-point self-similarity/cusp/tangent trichotomy.
within_source_synthesis_candidates.limit: The classification is proved for the specific regularity and coprimality conditions stated in the source, with a reduction when p divides the denominator.
